name: ID Migraine Screener

citations.text: Lipton RB, Dodick D, Sadovsky R, et al. A self-administered screener for migraine in primary care: The ID Migraine validation study. Neurology. 2003;61(3):375-382.

validated_population: Adults in primary care with two or more headaches in the past 3 months that interfered with work, school, or social life. Self-administered.
license_note: Published screening questions. Verify terms of use for the ID Migraine questionnaire before production deployment.

red_flags.question: Is this a sudden, severe headache that reached full strength within about 1 minute — the worst headache of your life?
red_flags.help: A sudden "thunderclap" headache can mean bleeding in the brain.

red_flags.question: Do you have a headache with fever and a stiff neck?
red_flags.help: Headache with fever and a stiff neck can mean meningitis.

red_flags.question: Did this headache start after a blow to the head?
red_flags.help: Use the head injury assessment instead, and get checked if the headache is severe or worsening.

red_flags.question: Are you pregnant or within 6 weeks after giving birth, with a new severe headache or vision changes?
red_flags.help: This can be a sign of high blood pressure in pregnancy (preeclampsia).

red_flags.question: Are you over 50 with a new type of headache plus jaw pain when chewing, scalp tenderness, or any vision change?
red_flags.help: These can be signs of giant cell arteritis, which can cause blindness if untreated.

items.question: During the last 3 months, did your headaches limit your ability to work, study, or do what you needed to do for at least 1 day?
items.help: Answer yes if a headache kept you from normal activities on at least one day.

items.question: During the last 3 months, did you feel nauseated or sick to your stomach when you had a headache?
items.help: Feeling like you might throw up counts.

items.question: During the last 3 months, did light bother you when you had a headache (a lot more than when you do not have headaches)?
items.help: Needing to avoid bright light during a headache.

scoring.threshold_text: 2 or 3 "yes" answers = positive screen for migraine; 0 or 1 = negative.

positive.label: Positive migraine screen
positive.interpretation: Your answers match the pattern of migraine. In the validation study, 93 in 100 people with a positive screen had migraine.
positive.recommendation: Book a primary care visit to confirm the diagnosis and discuss treatment and prevention.

ed_redirect: Headache with fever and stiff neck
New weakness, numbness, vision loss, or trouble speaking: call 911
self_care: Rest in a dark, quiet room during attacks.
Over-the-counter pain relievers early in an attack, no more than 2 to 3 days a week.
Keep a headache diary: dates, triggers, and treatments.

negative.label: Negative migraine screen
negative.interpretation: Your answers do not match the typical migraine pattern. Tension-type headache is the most common other cause.
negative.recommendation: Self-care. Book a visit if headaches are frequent or changing.

care.within: Self-care; primary care within 4 weeks if headaches happen 4+ days a month
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a primary care visit if headaches are frequent, getting worse, or you use pain relievers more than 2 to 3 days a week.
ed_redirect: Headache with fever and stiff neck
New weakness, numbness, vision loss, or trouble speaking: call 911
self_care: Over-the-counter pain relievers as labeled, no more than 2 to 3 days a week.
